microtheory.name: morphology_linguistics
microtheory.definition: Word structure and formation. Morphemes, inflection vs derivation, compounding, productivity. How languages create new words and modify existing ones. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional structure within lexical units — concepts can be decomposed + recomposed.

concepts.name: free_morpheme
concepts.definition: Stand-alone meaningful unit. 'Run', 'house', 'happy'. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic Concept.

concepts.name: bound_morpheme
concepts.definition: Cannot stand alone; attaches. -s, -ed, un-. Substrate analogue: substrate's modifier-only concept.

concepts.name: stem
concepts.definition: Core meaning-bearing part of a word, before affixes. Substrate analogue: substrate's root Concept.

concepts.name: root
concepts.definition: Smallest morpheme that bears core meaning. In 'unhappiness', 'happy' is root. Substrate analogue: substrate's primitive Concept.

concepts.name: affix
concepts.definition: Bound morpheme attaching to stem. Prefix, suffix, infix, circumfix. Substrate analogue: substrate's modifier edge.

concepts.name: inflection
concepts.definition: Morphology marking grammatical features (tense, number, case, agreement) on existing words. Doesn't change word class. Substrate analogue: substrate's grammatical-attribute marking.

concepts.name: derivation
concepts.definition: Morphology creating new words from existing ones. Often changes word class. 'Happy' → 'happiness' (Adj → N). Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-formation.

concepts.name: compounding
concepts.definition: Combining two free morphemes. 'Blackboard', 'firefly'. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-pair as new Concept.

concepts.name: reduplication
concepts.definition: Repeating part or all of a word for meaning change. Tagalog 'bili' (buy) → 'bibili' (will buy). Substrate analogue: substrate's repetition-as-meaning operation.

concepts.name: allomorph
concepts.definition: Phonologically-conditioned variants of a morpheme. English plural -s: /s/ after voiceless, /z/ after voiced, /əz/ after sibilant. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned form variants.

concepts.name: morphophonology
concepts.definition: Interface between morphology + phonology. Sound changes at morpheme boundaries. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional-phonological rules.

concepts.name: suppletion
concepts.definition: Irregular form replacing expected morphological derivation. 'Go/went', 'good/better'. Substrate analogue: substrate's exception-pattern.

concepts.name: productive_morpheme
concepts.definition: Can attach to new bases freely. '-ness' is productive; '-th' (warmth, length) is not. Substrate analogue: substrate's actively-generative pattern.

concepts.name: lexicalization
concepts.definition: Derived form becomes its own lexical item with idiosyncratic meaning. 'Hospital' originally from 'hospes'. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen compound Concept.

concepts.name: frequency_effects
concepts.definition: More frequent forms processed faster + retained better. Higher-frequency irregulars resist regularization. Substrate analogue: substrate's usage-frequency affecting Concept stability.

concepts.name: morphological_typology
concepts.definition: Languages classified by morphology: isolating (Chinese, few morphemes per word), agglutinative (Turkish, clear morpheme boundaries), fusional (Latin, multiple meanings per morpheme), polysynthetic (Inuktitut, sentences-as-words). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-language compositional density.

concepts.name: isolating_language
concepts.definition: One morpheme per word. Word order carries grammatical info. Chinese, Vietnamese. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic-Concept-per-word lexicon.

concepts.name: agglutinative_language
concepts.definition: Words built from multiple distinct morphemes. Turkish 'evlerimizden' = ev-ler-imiz-den (house-PL-our-from). Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree with clear constituents.

concepts.name: fusional_language
concepts.definition: Single morpheme carries multiple meanings. Latin 'amō' = love+1SG+PRES+IND. Substrate analogue: substrate's polymorphic Concept attributes.

concepts.name: polysynthetic_language
concepts.definition: Single word = full sentence. Inuktitut 'qangatasuukkuvimmuuriaqalaaqtunga'. Substrate analogue: substrate's complex compositional Concept.

concepts.name: morphological_paradigm
concepts.definition: Set of all inflected forms of a lexeme. Verb conjugation, noun declension. Substrate analogue: substrate's variant-set for a Concept.

concepts.name: syncretism
concepts.definition: Same form in different paradigm cells. Latin 'rosa' = nom/voc/abl singular. Substrate analogue: substrate's form-collision in Concept variants.

concepts.name: zero_morpheme
concepts.definition: Posited unmarked form contrasting with marked forms. English plural 'sheep' = 'sheep + ∅'. Substrate analogue: substrate's null-modifier concept.

rules.name: morphological_complexity_varies_typologically
rules.head: the substrate processes a language
rules.body: the morphological type (isolating to polysynthetic) determines whether to parse small words combined by syntax or long words with internal structure. Substrate's per-language parsing strategy.

rules.name: productive_patterns_generate_new_forms
rules.head: the substrate encounters a novel base
rules.body: productive morphological patterns (in English: -ness, -er, -ing) can attach freely. Non-productive ones (-th, -dom) cannot. Substrate's generative-pattern distinction.

rules.name: frequency_protects_irregularity
rules.head: the substrate processes an irregular form
rules.body: high frequency resists regularization pressure. 'Went' survives; 'wend' does not. Substrate's frequency-protected exception.

rules.name: morphophonological_rules_apply_at_boundaries
rules.head: the substrate composes morphemes
rules.body: phonological adjustments may occur at the boundary. English plural /s/ vs /z/ vs /əz/. Substrate's compositional phonological adaptation.

rules.name: compounding_creates_units_with_specialized_meaning
rules.head: the substrate combines two free morphemes
rules.body: the resulting compound often has meaning beyond the parts. 'Blackboard' isn't just any black board. Substrate's compound-Concept specialization.
